newsitem.title: UK: London court approves Berlusconi document transfer.
newsitem.headline: London court approves Berlusconi document transfer.

text.p: The London High Court on Wednesday approved the transfer of documents to the Italian authorities related to the business activities of Italian business tycoon and politician Silvio Berlusconi.
Britain's Serious Fraud Office seized 15 bags of documents earlier this year from the office of London lawyer David Mills who represents the interests of former Italian Prime Minister Berlusconi.

The judges, Lord Justice Simon Brown and Mr Justice Gage, rejected the grounds of an appeal, but Brown agreed to hear an application by the appellants on Friday morning, which could lead to an appeal to the House of Lords.

The hearing stemmed from an appeal by Berlusconi, who was Prime Minister of Italy for seven months in 1994 and is on trial in Milan on corruption charges, and his company Fininvest and others against a court ruling earlier this year that the papers should be sent to Italy.

The earlier hearing was told that the papers were linked to fraud and false accounting allegations amounting to 51 million pounds ($82 million) at overseas companies that were moved from Switzerland to England.

Italian investigators suspect Berlusconi who, among other holdings, owns three TV channels and the football club AC Milan, may have used offshore companies to channel payments to politicians. ($1=.6253 Pound)
